structured_output.what_is_happening: SHIBABRAIN is a pump.fun coin created about 29 hours before detection. It migrated to PumpSwap about 41 minutes before detection. After migration it pumped hard: about $1.04M of volume in the first hour, around 14.6k transactions and roughly 2.9k unique buyers. The all-time-high price (0.000875) puts the peak market cap near $875k. At detection it had already fallen about 69% from that peak, to about $270k, with -39% over 5 minutes and -61% over 15 minutes (GeckoTerminal). In the last 5 minutes unique sellers (300) outnumber unique buyers (279). This looks like the dump after a migration pump that has not yet found a floor. The pitch is 'first Shiba Inu with a scanned dog connectome brain trading on-chain', riding the brain-emulation/connectome AI meme. At least 9 copycat tokens with the same name appeared within about 35 minutes.

narrative.description: An AI and brain-emulation meme ('scanned dog connectome brain trading on-chain') attached to the Shiba brand. The story is novel and catchy. It is probably riffing on recent news about connectome scanning or brain uploads, but the packet can't confirm that.
narrative.why_spreading: A fast post-migration pump pulled in about 2.9k unique buyers and a wave of same-name clones within minutes. That shows real speculative attention, but it may already be past its peak for this cycle.

token_connection.why_this_token: It is the oldest pump.fun original among the active pairs (the pair was created first, the token was created about 29 hours earlier), it has a website and X account, and its market cap and liquidity are far above every clone.
token_connection.competing_tokens: About 9 same-name clones launched within 35 minutes of this pair. Several have near-zero liquidity (drained), and others sit at $11k-$55k market cap. One older ShibaBrain (HRkc...) is dead.

authenticity.evidence: There is broad participation: 2.9k unique buyers, 3.4k holders and a top-10 holding of about 21% (excluding pool and locker accounts). The dev holds about 0%, the dev wallet was funded from Bybit and has a prior best token around $875k ATH. LP is 100% burned and there are no paid DexScreener boosts. On the other side, GMGN tags 501 bundler wallets and 973 fresh wallets, the bot/degen rate is 42% and top bundler traders hold about 20%. That suggests a lot of engineered volume and bundled supply, and it is now being sold. There are 41 smart wallets and 3 renowned (KOL) wallets, which probably means KOL-driven flow that is already taking profit.
authenticity.uncertainty: There is no X data, so I can't tell whether KOL calls or organic posts drove the pump. It is also unclear who controls the Streamflow vault holding 9.58%.

structural_risks: Price is already -69% from ATH and still falling fast at detection. The entry comes 25 minutes later, possibly lower still.
Heavy bundler and fresh-wallet share (about 20% held by top bundlers) is overhead supply that can keep dumping.
The Streamflow vault holds 9.58% of supply; unlocks or the vault owner could add selling pressure.
Liquidity is about $47k against a $270k market cap, which is fine, but a 2x needs a return to about $540k+ market cap after a failed first wave.

structured_output.counterargument: The original of a catchy AI meme with around 3k buyers, a real website and X account, burned LP, a Bybit-funded dev with a track record and no dev holdings often gets a second leg after the first post-migration flush. From a flushed entry price, a retrace toward the $875k ATH would be more than a 2x. The clones show the market sees this as the canonical token, and 41 smart and 3 KOL wallets may re-bid the dip.
unknowns: Price at entry (25 minutes after detection): the dump may stop or continue

Whether the bundler wallets have finished exiting

structured_output.thesis: This is the canonical token of a catchy AI/connectome meme. Its structure is fairly clean (LP burned, dev holds nothing, no paid boosts), but the entry falls in the middle of a sharp post-migration dump: -69% from ATH and -61% over 15 minutes, with heavy bundler and bot participation. A liquidity pull is unlikely because the LP is burned, but the coin could bleed out and die. Getting back to about 2x from the entry needs a strong second wave. That is possible for a canonical meme, but less likely than further decay or a sideways drift that hits the -50% stop.
